subject: Post-call: workload reconciliation & POC success gates
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Aria Patel <aria@heliumai.com>, Devon Singh <devon.singh@heliumai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-25T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: workload reconciliation & POC success gates

Thanks again for taking the call today — appreciate the clarity on the HeliumAI use cases. Quick recap and a proposed lightweight intake so we can finalize the trial scope and timeline: please review and confirm the numbers below or flag differences. I attached a one‑page CSV (poc_workload_matrix.csv) you can edit directly.

Key POC objectives (proposed):
- Validate throughput at production-like concurrency for the 3 main endpoints (summarization, answer-retrieval, reranking).
- Meet latency SLOs: 95th percentile under 300ms for <512-token generations, under 600ms for long-form (512–2048 tokens) at target concurrency.
- Confirm output quality vs your internal evaluation set (precision on top-1 answers >= 88%).

Workload snapshot (please confirm):
- Summarization: avg tokens out 120, input tokens ~40; expected steady RPS 12, concurrency target 30; typical bursts to 180 RPS for 2–4 min.
- Answer-retrieval (contextual search + generation): avg tokens out 220, input tokens 200; steady RPS 6, concurrency 20; bursts 120 RPS for 1–2 min at peak of business hours.
- Reranking (short queries): avg tokens out 32, input tokens 20; steady RPS 40, concurrency 60; microbursts ~450 RPS lasting <30s during feature release.

Proposed POC timeline:
- Confirm workload matrix: by end of week (Jul 31).
- Prep & baseline run (Redwood infra + Helium sample data): Aug 3–5.
- Focused stress + quality runs: Aug 6–12.
- Readout & success decision: Aug 14.

Owners / next steps:
- Action: Aria — update the attached CSV with measured RPS and token-length percentiles, and drop sample inputs (sample_input_snippets.jsonl) into the Drive folder.
- Action: Ben — prepare probe plan and a short concurrency/latency matrix to exercise the bursts; will draft tomorrow.
- Action: Monica — lead rollout of the trial environment and confirm necessary network/VPC bits.

Open questions from our side:
1) Do you have a production estimate for number of distinct user sessions that generate the reranking microburst pattern?
2) Are there any hard block SLA requirements (e.g., regulatory retention) we should bake into the Private deployment?

Thanks — I’ll schedule a 30-min alignment next week (tentative Wed 8/4) after we get the matrix back.

Best,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Thanks — read the updates. A few suggested probe items based on those burst shapes and token percentiles:

Suggested probe plan (high level):
- Microburst probe: 30s ramp to 450 RPS against reranking endpoint with realistic session headers. Measure cold vs hot KV cache hit-rate.
- Sustained mid-run: 10 min @ 75% of steady RPS across all endpoints to observe memory growth and tail latencies.
- Long-token stress: targeted runs for the 95th token percentile (400–450 token outputs) to validate kernel selection and batching fallbacks.

Concurrency/latency knobs to exercise:
- Max concurrent requests per-worker: try 32, 64, 128 (we’ll watch latency curves).
- Aggressive prefix caching enabled for retrieval-heavy flows — should reduce tokens/second cost during sustained runs.

I’ve attached a short probe checklist (probe_plan.md) and will upload the step-by-step runner scripts to the shared Drive after we lock the matrix. For the PII constraint, Monica — we should confirm whether Helium wants token-level masking in-flight or to keep data on-prem during runs.

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

POC start window: Aug 3 (baseline) — target readout Aug 14.
Success gates (finalized):
1) Throughput: system sustains steady RPS with <= 10% error rate at target concurrency for each endpoint.
2) Latency: 95th percentile below thresholds noted earlier (<=300ms short; <=600ms long).
3) Quality: eval set top-1 precision >= 88% (Helium to provide labeled set by 7/27).
4) Data controls: agreed mitigation for PII during trial (Aria to confirm masking option or allow Private env).

- Redwood: Jonas (trial program lead), Ben (probe runs & artifacts), Monica (environment & network).
